evidence.note: Meanings: bring, bring up, command, fetch, guide, lead, look after, send; written forms ūrâ, ittarrû, arû.

cognates.note: Leading and guiding answer to the hiphil “point out the way, teach”, but the link rests on the meaning, and the Akkadian verb is not shown to mean throw.

evidence.note: “h pf hwry C318/4 MAKE KNOWN, ANNOUNCE (cf WRW h) … Heb torah ‘instruction’.”

evidence.note: “(ירי, Af. אוֹרִי = h. תּוֹרָה) instruction, the Law, Bible-verse. Targ. Lev. VI, 7; a. fr.”
“Af. of ירי.”

cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic of the Targums: the Aramaic noun for the law, from the aphel of the same root, rendering תּוֹרָה (Targ. Lev 6:7).

doctrine.statement: Isaiah and Micah see “the latter days” when many nations say, “Come, let us go up to the mountain of Yahweh … that he may teach us (וְיֹרֵנוּ) of his ways, and we will walk in his paths; for out of Zion shall go forth תּוֹרָה, and the word of Yahweh from Jerusalem”; he will judge between the nations, they will beat their swords into ploughshares, and nation will not learn war any more (Isa 2:2–4; Mic 4:1–3). The servant “will not grow faint … until he has set justice in the earth, and the coastlands wait for his תּוֹרָה” (Isa 42:4), and Matthew reads that servant as Jesus: “in his name the nations will hope” (Mat 12:18–21). From the verses: the teaching that went out from Sinai to Israel is to go out from Jerusalem to all nations, taught by Yahweh through his servant, in a rule on the earth under which war ends. That has not yet been, and waits for the servant to set justice in the earth.

Through Jeremiah Yahweh promised a new covenant unlike the one Israel broke: “I will put my תּוֹרָה within them, and write it on their heart, and I will be their God and they shall be my people” (Jer 31:31–33). Hebrews quotes it twice of the covenant Jesus mediates (Heb 8:6–10; 10:14–16). The psalmist who says “I delight to do your will, my God, and your תּוֹרָה is within my heart” (Psa 40:9) is read in Hebrews as Christ coming into the world (Heb 10:5–9), and “the law of his God is in his heart” is said of the righteous man (Psa 37:31). From the verses: the new covenant does not discard Yahweh's teaching but writes it within; Christ kept it so first, and those in the covenant through him are to have it so.

Jesus said that “everything written about me in the law of Moses and the prophets and the psalms must be fulfilled”, and opened their minds to understand the scriptures (Luk 24:44–45); he came “not to destroy the law or the prophets, but to fulfil” (Mat 5:17). The law itself pronounces: “Cursed is he who does not confirm the words of this תּוֹרָה by doing them” (Deu 27:26), and Paul quotes it to show that all who rest on the works of the law are under that curse, from which “Christ redeemed us, having become a curse for us” (Gal 3:10, 13); “the law was our tutor (παιδαγωγός) to bring us to Christ” (Gal 3:24). From the verses: the תּוֹרָה is a teaching in the plain sense of the word, and what it teaches points to Christ; it is fulfilled in him, not set aside.

“Good and upright is Yahweh; therefore he teaches sinners in the way” (Psa 25:8), and “who is a teacher like him?” (Job 36:22). Solomon asks forgiveness for Israel “for you teach them the good way in which they should walk”, in the same breath as “give rain on your land” (1Ki 8:36). Against him stand priests who “teach for hire” (Mic 3:11) and the idol, “a teacher of lies”: “Shall it teach? It is overlaid with gold and silver, and there is no breath in it at all” (Hab 2:18–19). From the verses: true teaching comes from the living God, and a teacher without his breath, wood or stone, teaches nothing.

gloss: throw, shoot; point out, teach; send rain; instruction, law
note: Drafted 2026-11-18 from `db lexicon-brief ירה`. Keys: תּוֹרָה j.di.af (219); verb j.di.aa; מוֹרֶה “teacher” j.di.ae; מוֹרֶה “early rain” j.di.ad; יוֹרֶה j.di.ac. BDB's j.dg.aa (יָרָא “shoot; pour”) lists the same surfaces as j.di.aa (the yare entry left it for this root), so only j.di.aa is named. Token counts undercount the verb badly: the morphology analyses about 77 of its tokens (Exo 4:12, Psa 25:8, Hos 6:3 and the rest) under root ירא, so `bdb_tokens` drops them as another root's verb and the verb shows about 13 uses, most of them in fact the nouns מוֹרֶה/יוֹרֶה filed by spelling; the true count is about 80. j.di.ae and j.di.ad overlap by spelling (Gen 12:6, Jol 2:23, Psa 84:7, Job 36:22). The place-name uses counted under j.di.ae have their own lexeme here. Left out: יְרוּשָׁלַיִם Jerusalem (j.dj.ab, 643): BDB files it under a separate homograph יָרַהּ, the city is a place (name entries take people), and the etymology (“foundation of Shalem”, from ירה “lay, set”, Job 38:6) is not shown by scripture: reviewer to decide whether it belongs here or needs its own entry. יָרַהּ “be stupified” (j.dj.aa, Isa 44:8 תִּרְהוּ, 0 tokens) is a form of רהה, not this root. Zero-token cross-references j.ba.ai, m.bc.ai, m.dk.ae, w.al.ae left out. The place יְרוּאֵל Jeruel (j.di.ah, 2Ch 20:16) left out. Names: drafted jorah, jeriah, jeriel. Not drafted: יוֹרַי Jorai (j.di.ag, 1Ch 5:13, TIPNR Jorai@1Ch.5.13): formed from the root but its meaning is not clear (“Yah teaches”? or a form of יוֹרֶה); reviewer to decide. Ketiv: 2Sa 11:24 וַיֹּרוּ הַמּוֹרִים is spelled with א in the ketiv (ויראו המוראים); 2Ch 26:15 לִירוֹא and Pro 11:25 יוֹרֶא are spellings with א. Cognates: Segert's Ugaritic page is p. 188 from the running heads (the head of that page is garbled in the OCR; p. 189 follows); not checked against the page image or DULAT. Ge'ez rests on Anderson–Moser and Wiktionary; Dillmann's column not looked up. Biella's Sabaic WRW I “fight, rebel” (p. 148, compared there with Ge'ez warawa “throw”) not recorded: the meaning is too far from the Hebrew to name on a word. Arabic: Lane's وري is “strike fire; hide; pretend” (p. 3052) and does not share any sense, so it is not recorded; Arabic تَوْرَاة “the Torah” is a borrowing from Hebrew/Aramaic and not recorded; Ge'ez ʾorit “the Law” likewise a borrowing (not checked in Dillmann). Wiktionary's Arabic رَوَى “transmit, relate” needs metathesis and was not followed. The SEDRA Peshitta lexicon has no ʾoraytā: the Peshitta New Testament says “law” with ܢܡܘܣܐ (from Greek νόμος), so the entry has no syc word. No Biblical Aramaic word of the root. The rain words (יוֹרֶה, מוֹרֶה, hiphil “water”, hophal) have no cognate that shares the rain sense; the tie to “throw/shoot” is an inference not yet shown by evidence. Open questions: (1) whether the verb's “teach” is a development of “throw/point” (as Gen 46:28, Exo 15:25 and Pro 6:13 suggest) or a second root that has merged with it; Akkadian warû and Sabaic hwry are possible only; (2) Jol 2:23 הַמּוֹרֶה לִצְדָקָה: early rain or teacher of righteousness.
summary: To throw or cast, and so to shoot an arrow, cast a lot or lay a stone in place; in the hiphil, to point out the way and so, most often, to teach. From the teaching comes תּוֹרָה, the instruction a father, a priest or a prophet gives and above all the law Yahweh gave by Moses, and from the one who gives it מוֹרֶה, the teacher. The same forms name the early rain (יוֹרֶה, מוֹרֶה), and scripture sets the two side by side: Yahweh teaches the good way and gives rain on the land (1Ki 8:36), and will come and rain righteousness (Hos 10:12). Ge'ez warawa “throw” shares the throwing, and the Aramaic of the Targums calls the law אוֹרָיְתָא from the same root.

senses.definition: Jerusalem is the city whose walls David asks Yahweh to build up.

evidence.note: Kings bring gifts to God in connection with his temple at Jerusalem.

words.summary: The traditional reading joins ירו־, a form associated with יָרָה, to שָׁלֵם, ‘peace’, but the name's full derivation is not established by Psalm 51. The city's identity and walls are certain in the cited verse.

words.gloss: instruction, teaching; a ruling; the law

evidence.locator: Psa.1.2, תּוֹרַת → νόμῳ; Isa.2.3, תוֹרָה → νόμος; Jer.31.33, תּוֹרָתִי → νόμους; Deu.27.26, הַתּוֹרָה → νόμου; Mal.3.22, תּוֹרַת → νόμου; νόμος renders תּוֹרָה ×189

evidence.note: Jer 31:33 quoted: “putting my laws (νόμους) into their mind, and I will write them on their hearts.” Also Heb 10:16.
Deu 27:26 quoted: “Cursed is everyone who does not continue in all things written in the book of the law (νόμου), to do them.”
“It is written in the law (νόμῳ) of Moses, You shall not muzzle an ox”: Deu 25:4.
“The law of Moses and the prophets and the psalms.”
“Do not think that I came to destroy the law (νόμον) or the prophets.”

senses.definition: What one person teaches another: a mother's or father's instruction to a son, the teaching of the wise, a prophet's message, set beside commandment, discipline and word.

evidence.note: “Hear, my son, the discipline (מוּסַר) of your father, and do not forsake the תּוֹרַת of your mother.”
“My son, do not forget my תּוֹרָה, and let your heart keep my commandments.”
“The commandment is a lamp and תּוֹרָה a light, and the reproofs of discipline the way of life.”
“The תּוֹרַת of the wise is a fountain of life, to turn from the snares of death.”
Of the capable wife: “the תּוֹרַת of kindness is on her tongue.”
Asaph: “Give ear, my people, to my תּוֹרָה; incline your ears to the words of my mouth.”
“Hear the word of Yahweh … give ear to the תּוֹרַת of our God”: the prophet's message, parallel to “word”.
“Bind up the testimony, seal the תּוֹרָה among my disciples.”
“To the תּוֹרָה and to the testimony! If they do not speak according to this word, there is no dawn for them.”
“Receive תּוֹרָה from his mouth, and lay up his words in your heart.”

senses.gloss: teaching, instruction (of parent, wise man, prophet)

senses.definition: A single instruction given for one matter: the procedure for an offering, the ruling on a skin disease or a vow, the decision a priest gives when asked. Often in the formula זֹאת תּוֹרַת “this is the instruction for …”, and in the plural, laws.

evidence.note: “Command Aaron … saying, זֹאת תּוֹרַת הָעֹלָה: it is the burnt offering on the hearth all night.”
“This is the תּוֹרָה for the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering …”
“To teach (לְהוֹרֹת) when it is unclean and when it is clean: this is the תּוֹרַת of the skin disease.” The verb and its noun together.
The תּוֹרַת of the Nazirite.
“One תּוֹרָה shall be for the native and for the sojourner among you.”
“Ask the priests תּוֹרָה, saying …”: a ruling sought on a case of holiness and uncleanness.
“According to the תּוֹרָה which they teach you (יוֹרוּךָ) and the judgment they say to you, you shall do.”
Moses makes known “the statutes of God and his תּוֹרֹת”.
Abraham “kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes and my תּוֹרֹת”.
“And this is the תּוֹרַת of man, Lord Yahweh”: David's wonder at the promise; the sense here is not clear.

senses.gloss: a ruling, the instruction for a case

senses.definition: The whole of Yahweh's instruction to Israel, given at Sinai by the hand of Moses, written in a book, kept beside the ark, read to the people and meditated on: “the law of Yahweh”, “the law of Moses”, “this law”.

evidence.note: “I will give you the tablets of stone, וְהַתּוֹרָה וְהַמִּצְוָה, which I have written לְהוֹרֹתָם, to teach them.”
“This is the תּוֹרָה which Moses set before the sons of Israel.”
The king is to write himself a copy of “this תּוֹרָה” in a book.
“Take this book of the תּוֹרָה and put it beside the ark of the covenant … as a witness against you.”
“Moses commanded us a תּוֹרָה, a possession for the assembly of Jacob.”
“This book of the תּוֹרָה shall not depart from your mouth; you shall meditate on it day and night.”
“I have found the book of the תּוֹרָה in the house of Yahweh.”
“They read in the book, in the תּוֹרַת of God, distinctly, and gave the sense.”
At Sinai Yahweh gave “right judgments and תּוֹרוֹת of truth, good statutes and commandments”.
“His delight is in the תּוֹרַת of Yahweh, and in his תּוֹרָה he meditates day and night.”
“The תּוֹרַת of Yahweh is perfect, restoring the soul.”
“How I love your תּוֹרָה! It is my meditation all the day.”
“You have forgotten the תּוֹרַת of your God.”
Judah “rejected the תּוֹרַת of Yahweh and did not keep his statutes”.
“Remember the תּוֹרַת of Moses my servant, which I commanded him at Horeb for all Israel.”
The manna: “that I may test them, whether they will walk in my תּוֹרָה or not.”
The new covenant: “I will put my תּוֹרָה within them and write it on their heart.” Quoted in Heb 8:10 and 10:16.
Jer 31:33 quoted: “putting my laws (νόμους) into their mind.”
“Everything written about me in the law (νόμῳ) of Moses and the prophets and the psalms must be fulfilled.”

senses.gloss: the law of Yahweh, given through Moses

senses.definition: In the prophets, Yahweh's teaching going out to the nations in the age to come: from Zion and Jerusalem, carried by his servant to the coastlands.

evidence.note: “That he may teach us (וְיֹרֵנוּ) of his ways … for out of Zion shall go forth תּוֹרָה, and the word of Yahweh from Jerusalem.”
The servant “will not grow faint … until he has set justice in the earth, and the coastlands wait for his תּוֹרָה”.
“תּוֹרָה will go out from me, and I will set my justice for a light of the peoples.”

senses.gloss: the instruction that goes out from Zion

senses.definition: The instruction the priest is charged to give from his mouth; its failure is the failure of the priesthood.

evidence.note: “The lips of a priest should keep knowledge, and they should seek תּוֹרָה from his mouth, for he is the messenger of Yahweh of armies.”
“The תּוֹרַת of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found on his lips.”
“תּוֹרָה shall not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet.”
“Her priests have profaned the holy; they have done violence to תּוֹרָה.”
Israel long “without a teaching priest (כֹּהֵן מוֹרֶה) and without תּוֹרָה”.

words.summary: About 220 times: what is taught, the noun of the hiphil “teach”. Scripture shows the link itself: “the תּוֹרָה which they teach you (יוֹרוּךָ)” (Deu 17:11), “they teach (יוֹרוּ) your judgments to Jacob and your תּוֹרָה to Israel” (Deu 33:10), the tablets “and the תּוֹרָה … that I have written to teach them (לְהוֹרֹתָם)” (Exo 24:12). It is a parent's or a wise man's teaching, the priest's ruling on a case, and above all the law of Yahweh given through Moses, written in a book and read to the people.

parallels.note: Commandment and teaching: the pair of Proverbs and of the Sinai tablets.
“The law of Yahweh” // “the testimony of Yahweh”; תְּעוּדָה in Isaiah.
A father's discipline // a mother's teaching.
“The word of Yahweh” // “the instruction of our God”.
Justice set in the earth // his teaching awaited.

words.gloss: throw, cast, shoot; point out, teach; send rain

stems.gloss: throw, cast; cast a lot; lay, set up; shoot

senses.definition: To hurl something away from oneself: an army into the sea, a lot before Yahweh.

evidence.note: “Pharaoh's chariots and his army יָרָה בַיָּם, he has cast into the sea.”
“וְיָרִיתִי לָכֶם גּוֹרָל here before Yahweh our God”: I will cast a lot for you.

senses.definition: To set a stone in its place: a cornerstone laid, a pillar set up.

evidence.note: “On what were its bases sunk, or who יָרָה its cornerstone?”
“Behold this heap and behold the pillar אֲשֶׁר יָרִיתִי between me and you.”

senses.definition: To send an arrow from the bow.

evidence.note: “Find the arrows which I shoot” (hiphil); “as the boy ran, he יָרָה the arrow beyond him.”
“The place of the arrow אֲשֶׁר יָרָה יְהוֹנָתָן.”
“The wicked bend the bow, they have set their arrow on the string, לִירוֹת in the dark at the upright in heart.”
Uzziah's engines “to shoot (לִירוֹא) arrows and great stones”; spelled with א.
Elisha: “יְרֵה, shoot!”, and he shot: “the arrow of Yahweh's deliverance.”
“וַנִּירָם, we have shot them; Heshbon has perished”: the reading of the song is not certain.

senses.definition: Of whatever touches the mountain at Sinai: put to death from a distance, by stone or arrow, without being touched.

evidence.note: “No hand shall touch him, but he shall surely be stoned or יָרֹה יִיָּרֶה, surely shot.”

stems.gloss: shoot; throw down; point out, show; teach, instruct; send rain

senses.definition: To shoot arrows, and as a noun the participle הַמּוֹרִים “the archers”; once, to throw down.

evidence.note: “I will shoot (אוֹרֶה) three arrows to the side of it, as though I shot at a mark.”
“The archers (הַמּוֹרִים), men with the bow, found him.”
“Did you not know that they would shoot from the wall?”
The king of Assyria “shall not come into this city, nor shoot an arrow there (וְלֹא־יוֹרֶה שָׁם חֵץ)”. Also Isa 37:33.
“But God shoots them (וַיֹּרֵם) with an arrow; suddenly they are wounded.”
“Like a madman who shoots (הַיֹּרֶה) firebrands, arrows and death.”
“The archers shot (וַיֹּרוּ הַיֹּרִים) at King Josiah.”
“He has cast me (הֹרָנִי) into the mire, and I have become like dust and ashes.”

senses.definition: To direct someone's eyes or steps to something: to show the way ahead, show a thing, point with the finger.

evidence.note: Jacob sent Judah ahead to Joseph “לְהוֹרֹת לְפָנָיו גֹּשְׁנָה”, to point out the way before him to Goshen.
“He cried to Yahweh, וַיּוֹרֵהוּ יַהְוֶה עֵץ, and Yahweh showed him a tree; he threw it into the water and the water became sweet.”
The worthless man “winks with his eyes, scrapes with his feet, מֹרֶה בְּאֶצְבְּעֹתָיו, points with his fingers”.

senses.definition: To show someone what to do or how to go: God teaching his way, a father his son, the priests Israel the difference between clean and unclean. The way (דֶּרֶךְ) is its commonest object, and it stands beside “make known”, “make understand” and “lead”.

evidence.note: “I will be with your mouth וְהוֹרֵיתִיךָ, and teach you what you shall speak.”
The law and commandment “which I have written לְהוֹרֹתָם, to teach them”.
The priests are “to teach (וּלְהוֹרֹת) the sons of Israel all the statutes which Yahweh has spoken to them by the hand of Moses”.
“Do according to all that they teach you (יוֹרוּךָ).”
Of Levi: “They shall teach (יוֹרוּ) your judgments to Jacob and your תּוֹרָה to Israel.”
“They shall teach (יוֹרוּ) my people the difference between holy and common, and make them know (יוֹדִעֻם) unclean from clean.”
Yahweh put it in Bezalel's heart “to teach”, he and Oholiab.
“Let the man of God come again to us וְיוֹרֵנוּ, and teach us what we shall do for the boy.”
Samuel: “I will teach you (וְהוֹרֵיתִי) the good and the right way.”
“For you teach them (תוֹרֵם) the good way in which they should walk, and give rain on your land.” Also 2Ch 6:27.
Jehoash did right “all his days, because Jehoiada the priest instructed him”.
A priest sent to Samaria “to teach them the custom of the God of the land”; v. 28, “how they should fear Yahweh”.
“That he may teach us (וְיֹרֵנוּ) of his ways, and we will walk in his paths.” Also Mic 4:2.
Of the farmer: “his God instructs him rightly; he teaches him.”
“Whom will he teach knowledge?”
“Good and upright is Yahweh; therefore he teaches (יוֹרֶה) sinners in the way.”
“הוֹרֵנִי יַהְוֶה דַּרְכֶּךָ, and lead me (וּנְחֵנִי) in a level path.”
“Teach me, Yahweh, the way of your statutes, and I will keep it to the end.”
“I will instruct you (אַשְׂכִּילְךָ) and teach you (וְאוֹרְךָ) in the way you should go.”
To the king: “your right hand shall teach you awesome things.”
“He taught me and said to me, Let your heart hold fast my words.”
“In the way of wisdom I have taught you.”
“Teach me (הוֹרוּנִי) and I will be silent; make me understand how I have erred.”
“Ask the beasts, and they will teach you.”
“Her priests teach for hire (בִּמְחִיר יוֹרוּ), and her prophets divine for money.”
“The prophet who teaches lies (מוֹרֶה שֶּׁקֶר), he is the tail.”
The molten image, “a teacher of lies”.
“Woe to him who says to the wood, Awake! … Shall it teach (הוּא יוֹרֶה)? It is overlaid with gold and silver, and there is no breath in it at all” (Hab 2:19).
“Without a teaching priest (כֹּהֵן מוֹרֶה) and without תּוֹרָה.”

senses.definition: Of rain, to water the land; of Yahweh, to rain righteousness on his people.

evidence.note: “He will come to us like the rain, like the latter rain that waters (יוֹרֶה) the land.”
“It is time to seek Yahweh, until he comes וְיֹרֶה צֶדֶק לָכֶם”: and rains righteousness on you. The verb is the one used for teaching.

senses.definition: Passive of the hiphil “water”: the generous man who waters others is watered himself.

evidence.note: “The generous soul will be made fat, and he who waters (מַרְוֶה) will himself be watered (יוֹרֶא).” Spelled with א.

words.summary: About eighty times. The qal throws: chariots into the sea, a lot before Yahweh, an arrow at a mark, a cornerstone laid. The hiphil, three times in four, points out the way and teaches: God, a father, priests, a prophet, even an idol. Throwing and teaching meet in pointing: Joseph is sent ahead “to point the way” (Gen 46:28), Yahweh “showed” Moses a tree (Exo 15:25), the worthless man “points with his fingers” (Pro 6:13). A few times the hiphil sends rain or waters, the sense of the nouns יוֹרֶה and מוֹרֶה “early rain”.

parallels.note: “Teach me your way … and lead me in a level path.”
“His God instructs him … he teaches him.”

senses.definition: One who teaches, a human teacher or God; beside מְלַמֵּד “instructor”.

evidence.note: “Behold, God is exalted in his power; who is a teacher (מוֹרֶה) like him?”
“I did not obey the voice of my teachers (מוֹרָי), nor incline my ear to my instructors (מְלַמְּדַי).”
“Your teacher will no longer be hidden, but your eyes shall see your teacher”; v. 21, “a word behind you: This is the way, walk in it.”

words.summary: The hiphil participle used as a noun, “one who teaches”. Yahweh is the teacher above all others (Job 36:22). The same spelling names places, the oak of Moreh at Shechem and the hill of Moreh, which may be named for a teacher or oracle there; scripture does not say.

evidence.locator: Deu.11.14, יוֹרֶה → πρόιμον; Jer.5.24, יוֹרֶה → πρόιμον

evidence.note: “The farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth … until it receives the early (πρόϊμον) and latter rain”: the pair of Deu 11:14.

senses.definition: The first rain of the year, given by Yahweh in its season with the latter rain.

evidence.note: “I will give the rain of your land in its season, יוֹרֶה וּמַלְקוֹשׁ, that you may gather your grain.”
“Let us fear Yahweh our God, who gives rain, יוֹרֶה וּמַלְקוֹשׁ, in its season.”

words.summary: The rain of autumn that opens the year's sowing, paired with מַלְקוֹשׁ, the latter rain of spring. Twice; the hiphil “water, send rain” (Hos 6:3) is the same form. No cognate yet shows a rain sense of the root, so its tie to “throw” rests on the hiphil's use only.

parallels.note: Early rain and latter rain, always together.

senses.definition: The autumn rain, with the latter rain.

evidence.note: “He has given you הַמּוֹרֶה לִצְדָקָה, and brought down for you the rain, מוֹרֶה וּמַלְקוֹשׁ, as before.”
“Passing through the valley of Baca they make it a spring; the early rain (מוֹרֶה) also covers it with blessings.”

words.summary: The same rain as יוֹרֶה, with the prefix מ. Twice or three times: in Joel 2:23 the first הַמּוֹרֶה לִצְדָקָה may be “the early rain for righteousness” or “the teacher of righteousness”, the spelling of מוֹרֶה “teacher”, and Hos 10:12 (“he will come and rain righteousness”) sets the same pairing of rain and righteousness. No cognate shows the rain sense.

senses.definition: The name identifying the oak at Shechem in Abram’s itinerary. Deuteronomy uses the same name with the plural “oaks.”

evidence.note: The second עַד specifies Abram’s destination at Shechem as אֵלוֹן מוֹרֶה, the oak of Moreh.
The oaks of Moreh serve as a landmark in the description of the location of Gerizim and Ebal.

senses.definition: The name of the hill used to locate the Midianite camp in the account of Gideon.

evidence.note: The narrator locates the camp by reference to גִּבְעַת הַמּוֹרֶה, the hill of Moreh.

words.summary: Moreh occurs in the names of a tree landmark at Shechem and a hill in the account of Gideon. Its form matches מוֹרֶה, “teacher,” but the passages leave the origin of the name open.
